question: What does CSS stand for in web design? 🌐
explanation: Brilliant! CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, which describes how HTML elements are to be displayed on screen. 🚀
hint: Think of a waterfall 'cascading' down!

question: Which HTML tag is used to define an internal style sheet? 📄
explanation: Spot on! The <style> tag is placed inside the <head> section to write internal CSS. 👍
hint: It is the very word we use for designing!

question: Which HTML attribute is used to apply inline styles directly to an element? 🎯
explanation: Fantastic! The 'style' attribute is used directly inside an HTML tag to apply inline CSS. ⚡
hint: It shares its name with the tag used for internal CSS!

question: Which property is used to change the background color of an element? 🖼️
explanation: Great job! The 'background-color' property colors the background of any HTML element. 🌟
hint: It has two words joined by a hyphen.

question: Which CSS property is used to change the text color? ✍️
explanation: Awesome! In CSS, 'color' is used to set the text (foreground) color. ✨
hint: It is just one simple word.

question: How do you select an element with id='header' in CSS? 🆔
explanation: Perfect! The hash symbol (#) is used to select an element by its unique ID. 🎯
hint: Look for the symbol often called a hashtag.

question: How do you select elements with class='menu' in CSS? 🏷️
explanation: Excellent! A period or dot (.) is used to select elements with a specific class. 🌟
hint: It starts with a tiny dot!

question:
What is the correct CSS syntax to make all

elements bold? 🅰️
explanation: Superb! The 'font-weight' property is used to make text thicker or bolder. 🏆
hint: Think about the 'weight' of the font!

question: Which property removes the underline from a hyperlink? 🔗
explanation: Outstanding! We use 'text-decoration: none;' to remove the default underline from <a> tags. 🎉
hint: We are removing a 'decoration' from the text.

question: Which property is used to change the font of an element? 🔤
explanation: Nice work! The 'font-family' property specifies the typeface to be used. 🌟
hint: Fonts come in 'families' (like Arial, Times New Roman).

question: Which CSS property controls the text size? 📏
explanation: Bingo! 'font-size' determines how large or small your text appears. 🎯
hint: We are measuring the 'size' of the font.

question: Which tag is used to link an external CSS file? 🔗
explanation: Awesome! We use the <link> tag inside the <head> to connect an external stylesheet. ✨
hint: We want to 'link' the files together.

question: Where should the <link> tag be placed in an HTML document? 📄
explanation: Correct! External stylesheets should always be linked inside the <head> section of HTML. 🌟
hint: It goes in the top 'brain' part of the HTML document.

question: What is the correct CSS syntax to center-align text? ⚖️
explanation: Brilliant! The 'text-align' property determines the horizontal alignment of text. 🎉
hint: You are 'aligning' the 'text'.

question: Which property is used to add space inside the border of an element? 📦
explanation: Excellent! Padding creates space INSIDE the element's border. 🎈
hint: Think of bubble wrap inside a shipping box.

question: Which property is used to add space outside the border of an element? 🛑
explanation: Superb! Margin creates space OUTSIDE the element's border, pushing other elements away. 🚀
hint: Think of the blank edges of a notebook page.

question: How do you add a comment in a CSS file? 💬
explanation: Spot on! CSS uses the /* */ syntax for writing comments that the browser ignores. 🌟
hint: It uses a slash and an asterisk.

question: Which selector applies styles to all elements on a page? 🌍
explanation: Perfect! The asterisk (*) is the universal selector that targets every single element. ✨
hint: It is the 'star' symbol!

question: Which CSS property makes text italic? 🤌
explanation: Great job! The 'font-style' property is used to make text italic or oblique. 🎉
hint: It changes the 'style' of the font.

question: What is the default value of the 'position' property? 📍
explanation: Awesome! By default, all HTML elements have a static position, flowing naturally down the page. ⚡
hint: It means staying in the normal flow, not moving.

question: How do you select all <h1> elements on a page? 📝
explanation: Fantastic! To select an HTML element directly, just type its tag name without any dots or hashes. 🚀
hint: Just use the tag name itself.

question: Which property sets the thickness of a border? 📏
explanation: Brilliant! We use 'border-width' to specify how thick or thin a border should be. ✨
hint: Think of the 'width' of the line.

question: Which value of 'border-style' creates a dotted line? ⚪
explanation: Spot on! The 'dotted' value creates a border made of tiny dots. 🌟
hint: The name is exactly what it looks like!

question: Which property is used to set an image as the background? 🖼️
explanation: Excellent! The 'background-image' property loads an image into the background of an element. 🎉
hint: It's two words joined by a hyphen, starting with background.

question: How do you specify the color 'red' for a border? 🔴
explanation: Superb! 'border-color' is the specific property used to paint the border a certain color. 🚀
hint: You are coloring the border!

question: Which of these is a valid CSS color value? 🎨
explanation: Perfect! CSS allows colors to be defined by HEX codes, RGB values, or standard color names. 🌟
hint: All three methods are perfectly fine!

question: In the rule 'p { color: blue; }', what is 'p'? 🎯
explanation: Awesome! 'p' is the selector because it 'selects' the HTML elements you want to style. ✨
hint: It 'selects' the element!

question: In the rule 'p { color: blue; }', what is 'color'? 🎨
explanation: Great job! 'color' is the property you are changing for the selected element. 🎉
hint: It is the specific feature you want to change.

question: What is the highest priority CSS? 🥇
explanation: Brilliant! Inline CSS has the highest priority and will override internal and external styles. 🚀
hint: The one written directly inside the HTML tag!

question: Which extension is used to save an external CSS file? 💾
explanation: Outstanding! External stylesheets must be saved with a .css file extension. 🌟
hint: It's just the three letters of the language!

question: If multiple classes are applied to an element, how are they separated in the HTML class attribute? 🏷️
explanation: Spot on! In HTML, you separate multiple class names inside the class attribute with a simple space. ✨
hint: Just leave a blank gap between them.

question: What CSS property makes a font uppercase? 🔠
explanation: Fantastic! We use 'text-transform: uppercase;' to change text to capital letters. 🎉
hint: You are 'transforming' the text.

question: Which value for 'background-repeat' prevents an image from repeating? 🚫
explanation: Excellent! Setting 'background-repeat: no-repeat;' ensures the image only appears once. 🚀
hint: Think 'no' to repeating.

question: Which is the shorthand property for setting all border properties at once? 📦
explanation: Superb! The 'border' property lets you set width, style, and color all in one line. 🌟
hint: It is just the basic word.

question: How do you make text appear with a strike-through? <s>
explanation: Awesome! 'text-decoration: line-through;' draws a line right through the middle of the text. ✨
hint: It draws a line 'through' it.

question: Can you use both a class and an ID on the same HTML element? 🤔
explanation: Perfect! An element can have both an ID (for unique styling/scripting) and classes (for shared styling). 🎉
hint: There are no rules against using both together!

question: What is the correct syntax for an ID selector named 'header'? 🆔
explanation: Great job! ID selectors always start with a hashtag (#) in CSS. 🚀
hint: IDs use the pound/hash symbol.

question: Which property controls the space between letters? 🔠
explanation: Brilliant! 'letter-spacing' adjusts the horizontal space between individual characters. 🌟
hint: You are spacing out 'letters'.

question: Which property controls the space between words? 📝
explanation: Spot on! 'word-spacing' is used to increase or decrease the white space between words. ✨
hint: You are spacing out 'words'.

question: What happens if a CSS property is spelled incorrectly? 🐛
explanation: Fantastic! Browsers are forgiving; if they don't understand a CSS rule, they just skip it and move on. 🎉
hint: Browsers just pretend they didn't see it!

question: What CSS property gives an element rounded corners? 🔄
explanation: Excellent! 'border-radius' curves the sharp corners of an HTML element's border box. 🚀
hint: Think of the 'radius' of a circle.

question: Which CSS syntax is correct for grouping selectors? 🤝
explanation: Superb! You can group selectors by separating them with commas to apply the same styles to multiple elements. 🌟
hint: Use a common punctuation mark used for lists.

question: In the CSS box model, what comes right outside the 'content'? 📦
explanation: Awesome! In the Box Model, Padding wraps the content, Border wraps the padding, and Margin is on the outside. ✨
hint: It's the cushion right next to the content.

question: How do you make a list NOT display bullet points? 📋
explanation: Perfect! 'list-style-type: none;' removes the default bullets or numbers from lists. 🎉
hint: You are modifying the 'list style'.

question: What is the correct CSS to change the background color of the whole page? 🌍
explanation: Great job! To style the entire visible page background, we apply the background-color to the <body> tag. 🚀
hint: Target the main container where all visible content lives.

question: Which unit is relative to the font-size of the root element? 📏
explanation: Brilliant! 'rem' stands for Root EM, meaning it scales relative to the main root (usually HTML) font size. 🌟
hint: It starts with an 'r' for root.

question: What is the correct way to specify a fallback font? 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
explanation: Spot on! You specify multiple fonts separated by commas. If the first fails, the browser tries the next one. ✨
hint: Just list them using commas.

question: Which of these overrides all other CSS rules? 👑
explanation: Fantastic! Appending '!important' to a CSS value forces it to override all other conflicting rules. 🎉
hint: It marks the rule as highly 'important'!

question: Which CSS property is used to make an image transparent? 👻
explanation: Excellent! The 'opacity' property changes the transparency level of an element from 0.0 (invisible) to 1.0 (solid). 🚀
hint: It defines how opaque something is.

question: Which attribute points to the external CSS file in the <link> tag? 📍
explanation: Awesome! We use the 'href' (hypertext reference) attribute in the <link> tag to point to our .css file. 🌟
hint: It's the same attribute used in <a> tags for links!
